rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes a nitridation treatment to form a CrN diffusion barrier at the Cr/Zr interface, whereas the target paper uses DC magnetron-sputtered AlTiCrZrNbTa high-entropy alloy coatings with varying Al content. These are fundamentally different interventions: one is a surface treatment of an elemental Cr coating, the other is a compositional variation of a multi-element alloy coating.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis mentions testing under high-temperature steam and subcritical-water conditions, while the target paper uses isothermal oxidation in flowing steam at 1000 °C for 60 min and 1100 °C for 30 min. The hypothesis lacks the specific temperature, time, and steam flow conditions of the target, and includes subcritical-water testing not present in the target.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis relies on a CrN diffusion barrier to limit Cr–Zr interdiffusion, whereas the target paper's mechanism involves preferential nucleation of Al2O3, TiO2, and Cr2O3 to form a dense composite oxide layer that suppresses oxygen diffusion, with excess Al causing intermetallic formation and oxide discontinuity. These are entirely different mechanisms.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts reduced interfacial diffusion and improved durability in steam, while the target paper predicts and measures a minimum oxidation rate and oxygen penetration at an intermediate Al content (~10 at.%) with degraded performance at higher Al. The predicted property (interdiffusion rate vs. oxidation mass gain) and direction differ.
